# The ticket store must be mutated through rebar, never through git stash

`_store/push.py` performs a stash -> merge -> pop dance inside the tickets worktree (module
docstring, bug 12a6), with `_resolve_conflicted_pop` (push.py:167-200) to repair a pop that
applies with conflict (bug 6818). It ends by dropping the stash (push.py:200).

## Why the design is unsound
Its stated assumption is that "the stashed working-tree edits live on reconciler-REGENERABLE
files" (push.py:170-176). That assumption does not hold, because **git's stash stack is shared
across every worktree of a repository**. `.tickets-tracker` is a LINKED WORKTREE of
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git`, and this machine currently has ELEVEN worktrees on that repo.
A `git stash pop` executed in the tickets worktree can therefore pop a stash created in a
SOURCE worktree.

## Observed incident
A stash created on branch `fix-c5b3-scc-byfile` was popped into the tickets worktree:

    stash@{0}: On fix-c5b3-scc-byfile: RECOVERED measurement-provenance work
    (ADR 0061 / det_measurement_provenance) displaced into worktree fix-c5b3-scc-byfile
    by a shared-stash race; backup at /tmp/RECOVERED-stash-race

Its contents are exactly the two paths that kept conflicting in the tracker:
    .rebar/criteria_routing.json            +23
    src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py  +9
Neither is reconciler-regenerable; both are source. Effects:
- SOURCE files (src/, docs/, tests/, .rebar/) appeared in the tickets worktree, which tracks
  no source tree at all — origin/tickets is clean, so this is purely local corruption.
- The index was left with unmerged (DU) entries and NO MERGE_HEAD — a stranded state that
  blocks EVERY ticket write. It oscillated (4 unmerged -> 0 -> 4) as concurrent rebar
  operations popped and re-stashed, so manual cleanup did not hold.
- It blocked the close of bug beb1 whose completion verification had already PASSED, and
  caused two COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecars to be lost ("could not be written").
- The stash message records that this race had ALREADY displaced work once before.

## Principle
The ticket system is an event-sourced store with its own API. It must be mutated through
rebar, not by direct filesystem/git manipulation of the tracker worktree. `git stash` in
particular is a REPO-GLOBAL operation being used for worktree-local intent, which is the
category error here.

(For the record: agents have also been doing direct git in the tracker — this session used
`git add -A` / `commit` / `merge` / `push` / `rm` there during a remediation. That is the same
violation from the other direction and should also be designed out, e.g. a locked
commit-and-push entrypoint that agents use instead.)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] rebar performs NO `git stash` operation in the tickets worktree. Replace the
      stash->merge->pop dance with a mechanism that cannot touch a shared, repo-global stack —
      e.g. commit-then-merge on the tickets branch, a worktree-scoped temporary ref, or a
      `git -c stash.useBuiltin` free path that stages into a dedicated ref.
- [x] If any stash-like step is unavoidable, it must be provably scoped so it can never apply
      a stash entry created by another worktree/branch (assert the stash's branch-of-origin
      before popping, and refuse otherwise).
- [x] Held-out test: with an unrelated stash created on a DIFFERENT branch of the same repo,
      a tickets-store write that hits the push-retry path must not apply it and must not
      strand the index.
- [x] `_resolve_conflicted_pop`'s regenerable-files assumption is either enforced or removed.
- [x] fsck (or the store write path) reports a tickets worktree containing tracked-source
      paths, since origin/tickets legitimately has none.
